How to Discover a Leak Location?

Plumbing leaks are unfortunately quite a common issue. In the vast majority of cases, they are not particularly dangerous as long as they’re addressed in good time. However, sometimes the leak location is not visible to the naked eye which can lead to the problem not being discovered for quite a long time. This can lead to the accumulation of a lot of water damage, mold and mildew growth, and in particularly severe cases, structural damage to the property.

If you notice persistent damp smells, discoloration on the walls, or the sounds of dripping or running water coming from behind the walls, it may be a good idea to get in touch with a professional. Remember — when it comes to leak detection it’s always better to be safe than sorry.

Leak Detection FAQs
What are the signs that I need plumbing leak detection?

Common signs of a hidden plumbing leak include unexplained increases in water usage, damp or discolored walls, peeling paint or wallpaper, musty odors, wet flooring, and the sound of running water when fixtures are turned off. Professional plumbing leak detection can help locate the source before additional water damage occurs.
How does professional water leak detection work?

Professional water leak detection uses diagnostic methods to narrow down the location of a hidden plumbing leak without relying only on visible damage. The appropriate method depends on where the leak is suspected and whether it involves a water line, pipe behind a wall, or another part of the plumbing system.
Can a plumber find a hidden water leak without opening walls?

In many cases, a plumber can use leak detection equipment and diagnostic testing to narrow down the source of a hidden water leak before opening a wall or other finished surface. Once the location is identified, the plumber can determine what access and repairs are necessary.
Do leak detection services include leak repair?

Leak detection identifies the location and potential cause of a plumbing leak so the appropriate repair can be recommended. Depending on the location and extent of the problem, repairs may involve a specific section of pipe or a larger plumbing repair when more extensive damage is found.
